source_text: V. Martianus ait: Omnium trade mihi nomina. respondit Achatius: Nomina eorum caelesti libro et divinis paginis sunt annotata. quomodo ergo oculi mortales aspicient quod immortalis virtus dei et invisibilis annotavit? Martianus ait: Ubi sunt magi, socii artis tuae vel doctores huius artificiosae fallaciae? respondit Achatius: Nos omnia meruimus a deo et meremur, sectam vero magicae artis horremus. Martianus ait: Ideo magi estis quia novum nescio quod genus religionis inducitis. respondit Achatius: Illos destruimus quos vos prius facitis et a vobis factos ipsi timetis. deficient enim vobis dii, si artifex saxo, aut saxum non abundaret artifici. timemus enim nos illum, non quem fabricamus, sed a quo fabricati sumus; qui nos creavit ut dominus, amavit ut pater, et aeternae morti, quasi bonus patronus, eripuit.
pass_a_gloss: Martianus says: Hand over to me the names of all. Achatius answers: Their names have been written down in a heavenly book and in divine pages; how then shall mortal eyes look upon what the immortal and invisible power of God has written down? Martianus says: Where are the magicians, the partners of your craft or the teachers of this cunning deceit? Achatius answers: We have obtained all things from God and do obtain them, but we abhor the sect of the magical art. Martianus says: You are magicians for this reason, because you bring in some new kind of religion or other. Achatius answers: We destroy those whom you first make and, once made by you, you yourselves fear; for gods will fail you if either the craftsman should lack stone or stone should lack a craftsman. For we fear not him whom we fashion, but him by whom we were fashioned, who created us as Lord, loved us as Father, and, as a good protector, snatched us from eternal death.
pass_b_english: Martianus said: Hand over to me the names of them all.
Achatius answered: Their names have been entered in a heavenly book and on divine pages.
How then shall mortal eyes behold what the immortal and invisible power of God has written?
Martianus said: Where are the sorcerers, the partners in your craft, or the teachers of this cunning fraud?
Achatius answered: All that we have, we have received from God and still receive, but we abhor the school of the magic art.
Martianus said: You are sorcerers for this reason, because you are introducing some new kind of religion or other.
Achatius answered: We destroy those gods whom you first make yourselves and then, once made by you, fear yourselves.
For gods will fail you if the craftsman runs short of stone, or stone runs short of a craftsman.
For we fear not him whom we fashion, but him by whom we were fashioned, who created us as Lord, loved us as Father, and, as a good protector, rescued us from eternal death.

choices.english: hand over to me the names
choices.why: trade is second-person singular present imperative of trado, with mihi as indirect object, so a command to produce the list, not merely to speak

choices.english: in a heavenly book and in divine pages
choices.why: ablative of place where with annotata sunt, plural libros/pages emphasizing a divine register contrasted with mortal eyes
quasi with noun gives role or likeness, and patronus here is protector/advocate rather than legal owner, fitting eripuit from death
